title.value: Reassessing Evaluation Practices in Visual Question Answering: A Case Study on Out-of-Distribution Generalization
title.justification: The title is directly provided in the paper, containing key details about its focus on VQA and OOD generalization.
title.quote: Reassessing Evaluation Practices in Visual Question Answering: A Case Study on Out-of-Distribution Generalization

extractions.description: This paper investigates the generalization capabilities of pretrained Visual Question Answering (VQA) models beyond their training datasets. It evaluates how well these models perform on out-of-distribution (OOD) datasets to determine if they are truly learning to solve the task of VQA or just optimizing for specific benchmarks. The study finds that these models exhibit poor OOD generalization, suggesting they are more adept at performing specific benchmarks rather than acquiring the broader skill necessary for VQA. The research also evaluates the impact of multimodal pretraining, automatic evaluation metrics, and compares performance between generative and discriminative models.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper focuses on the evaluation practices and generalization of VQA models, specifically their performance on OOD datasets. While this work may indirectly impact development by improving AI models' robustness, sustainable development in climate or ecological contexts is not a central theme.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: In this work, we investigate if recent pretrained VQA models can indeed answer any open-ended question about images or if they are mostly suitable for answering questions from the VQA benchmarks they are optimized for.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any categories listed under Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. Instead, it focuses on AI model evaluation and generalization.
primary_category.quote: The quality of such models is commonly assessed by measuring their performance on unseen data that typically comes from the same distribution as the training data. However, when evaluated under out-of-distribution (out-of-dataset) settings for VQA, we observe that these models exhibit poor generalization.

applications.value: Evaluation of VQA models on out-of-distribution datasets
applications.justification: The paper focuses on evaluating VQA models' performance on datasets not seen during training, highlighting the potential to understand models' real-world applicability beyond benchmark datasets.
applications.quote: In this work, we extensively evaluate OOD generalization of current pretrained V&L models by conducting cross-dataset evaluations.

applications.value: Comparing generative and discriminative approaches in VQA
applications.justification: The research compares different modeling approaches to understand which are more effective in generalizing beyond training datasets.
applications.quote: In most cases, we observe that generative models—which are not bound to predictions over a fixed set of answers curated from the training data—are more robust to OOD evaluation than discriminative ones.
